source.title: Batch normalization provably avoids ranks collapse for randomly initialised deep networks
source.authors: Hadi Daneshmand; J. Kohler; F. Bach; T. Hofmann; Aurélien Lucchi

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures hidden-representation rank and training performance under depth, batch normalization, and initialization changes. These experiments bear on the training behavior in V1, V3, and V6, but do not use the exact datasets and model settings specified by all versions.
record.gate_note: Training accuracy and loss are reported alongside rank. The paper also reports rank-only results; those do not by themselves measure the training behavior in the claim. The cited results of other studies are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures training accuracy and loss under normalization and initialization changes, bearing on V1, V4 and V6. It does not test V3's depth comparison between plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and identity-shortcut counterparts.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors prove rank preservation under technical assumptions for deep linear BN networks, demonstrate related behavior empirically for ReLU networks, and argue that initial representation rank strongly affects subsequent optimization. Rank-increasing preparation improves plain-network training, while positive asymmetric initialization undermines BN networks' rank and training performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study focuses on representation rank under random initialization and BN, with training-performance experiments on Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10. It does not directly reproduce the claim’s benchmark and recipe combinations.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth, batch normalization, initialization symmetry/centering, and rank-increasing pretraining are shown to affect rank or training performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Unnormalized Fashion-MNIST MLPs become difficult to train above approximately ten layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Plain ReLU MLPs can suffer depth-dependent training failure within a fixed training budget.

fits_no_version.finding: BN preserves representation rank at initialization, whereas unnormalized linear networks can collapse toward rank one even with fixed-strength residual connections.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization and initialization govern representation-rank preservation in deep random networks; identity shortcuts with fixed branch strength need not prevent rank collapse.

fits_no_version.finding: Rank-pretrained plain MLPs can converge faster than BN MLPs at the tested depths.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rank-increasing preparation can outperform BN for optimization in the tested MLP settings; this is an alternative recipe beyond V6's same-network normalization comparison and its specific Fixup exception.

record.problems: Several training-accuracy results are presented only as plots without numerical values. The experiments use a small number of independent runs (5 for the cited plots), and the reported Fashion-MNIST depth results are not on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100.
record.rows_left_out: Rank-only results from Figures 2-3 and 6-9, centering comparisons in Figure 7, gradient-angle and random-data comparisons in Figure 10, and pretraining-versus-BN curves in Figures 4, 11, and 12 were not included because they do not directly measure a version’s stated training-error claim or its specific BN speed comparison. ResNet50 initialization results in Figure 13 are figure-only and training accuracy values are not described in the text.

untested.parts: Random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, Adam, systematic capacity scaling, and eventual convergence after longer training.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious-local-minimum frequencies, and extra student neurons.
Training-error comparisons across depth for plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and identity-shortcut networks, longer-training controls, and the tanh and Fixup exceptions.
Activation-matched variance prescriptions, direct signal- and gradient-norm preservation comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh initialization, and training 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Higher-learning-rate tolerance, the named sigmoid-MNIST and Inception-ImageNet settings, and the Fixup recipe.

missing.what: Figure 6 includes supervised training loss, despite the record describing it as rank-only. Extract separate standard-initialization and 25- and 75-iteration rank-pretraining conditions for depth-32, width-128 Fashion-MNIST MLPs. The text explicitly connects greater preparation with better optimization; the vertical axis says training loss despite the caption saying accuracy.
missing.locator: Section 4, 'Rank through the optimization process'; Figure 6; Appendix G

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for these versions. Figure 10 also reports a direct VGG19 BN-versus-no-BN training comparison, including failure without BN despite a 100-fold learning-rate increase; it bears on V6, but its omission was explicitly declared in rows_left_out. Figures 4, 11–13 likewise have declared omissions. Rank alone does not establish training speed, training error, or the success of residual shortcuts.

versions.untested_parts: Random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-100, and Adam are not tested. The reported comparisons use Fashion-MNIST or CIFAR-10.

The study does not compare plain and identity-shortcut convolutional networks across depth as described in the version. It reports depth results for Fashion-MNIST MLPs and CIFAR-10 MLPs, plus initialization changes in VGG19 and ResNet50.
The study does not test sigmoid MNIST, VGG CIFAR-10 against a network without BN for training speed, Inception ImageNet, or Fixup.

rows.subject: ReLU multilayer perceptrons (MLPs)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD for 75 epochs while varying depth; no batch normalization.
rows.value: Vanilla networks are essentially unable to learn when the number of layers is above 10, in a limited number of epochs.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and 95% confidence interval of 5 independent runs; numerical values are figure only.
rows.note: The text describes the depth trend but gives no exact accuracy values. The benchmark is Fashion-MNIST, outside the named benchmarks in V1.
rows.check: The reported learning failure is supported, but Fashion-MNIST MLPs do not measure V1's convolutional-network claim or V3's batch-normalized convolutional depth comparison. No initialization comparison tests V4 in this row.

source_check.locator_found: Section 1.1; Figure 1 caption and right panel.

rows.subject: ReLU multilayer perceptrons (MLPs)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD for 75 epochs while varying depth; batch normalization included.
rows.baseline: Vanilla networks at corresponding depths; exact values not stated.
rows.value: Training accuracy drops only very mildly as depth reaches 32.
rows.uncertainty: Mean and 95% confidence interval of 5 independent runs; numerical values are figure only.
rows.note: The study explicitly describes the BN accuracy trend. Exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Compared with R1, BN preserves much higher training accuracy within the same 75-epoch budget at greater depths. Remove V1 and V3: these are Fashion-MNIST MLPs, without a residual-shortcut comparison. This measures accuracy gained within a fixed budget, not learning-rate tolerance.

source_check.locator_found: Section 1.1; Figure 1 caption and right panel.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with batch normalization and standard PyTorch initialization.
rows.uncertainty: Average and 95% confidence interval of 5 independent runs; figure-only values.
rows.note: The text identifies this as the standard-initialization BN comparison but does not describe its numerical accuracy.
rows.check: The supplied figure text does not establish whether training error reaches near zero. There is no depth comparison for V3 or BN-versus-no-BN comparison for V6.

rows.subject: VGG19
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with batch normalization and asymmetric uniform initialization of the same variance.
rows.baseline: Standard PyTorch initialization; exact values not stated.
rows.value: Even VGG networks are unable to fit CIFAR-10 after this initialization change.
rows.uncertainty: Average and 95% confidence interval of 5 independent runs; figure-only values.
rows.locator: Figure 5, left panel; Section 4, “Breaking batch normalization”
rows.note: Authors explicitly report failure to fit after the initialization change; plotted accuracy values are not stated.
rows.check: The authors explicitly report failure to fit CIFAR-10 under positive, same-variance random initialization. This is absence of near-zero training error within the reported run, not a reversed effect. Remove V3 and V6: neither the required depth comparison nor a normalization control is present. The figure covers approximately eight epochs, so it does not establish eventual failure.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4, Breaking batch normalization; Figure 5 caption, legend and epoch axis.

relationships.condition: Batch-normalized VGG19 on CIFAR-10 with positive uniform initialization, within approximately eight epochs
relationships.reason: R4 reports failure to fit after shifting the initialization to positive weights at unchanged variance; this qualifies initialization and training-budget scope without establishing eventual nonconvergence.
relationships.display_finding: Shifting weights to positive values while preserving variance prevented fitting within the tested budget.
